keys.meaning: Race phase, percentage distance, integer remaining distance or elapsed race seconds.
Skills that activated in the named part of the race. The opening phase includes start activations, not only the tick-0 instant. Lower skill IDs can trigger higher IDs on the same timestamp.
keys.limitation: The replay event list is the activation record. A skill with no event did not activate.

keys.meaning: Preselected random activation window within the named phase/course region.
keys.limitation: Being in the candidate region does not prove the selected random window coincided with other conditions.

gametora.reviewNote: There are four random corner-point draws; a short cooldown can allow repeated activations. Candidate regions do not reveal the actual draws.

keys.meaning: Unconditional reference predicate.

Gap to the immediately adjacent runner in rank order, in horse lengths (2.5 m).
Continuous proximity to any runner within 2.5 m and one horse lane; own rank changes reset the timer, replacement neighbors do not.
keys.limitation: GameTora reference spatial policy; sample-held timers may differ from hidden between-sample transitions.

gametora.reviewNote: Any qualifying runner can sustain proximity: at most 2.5 m longitudinally and one horse lane laterally. A change in this runner’s rank resets the timer; replacing the nearby runner does not.

keys.meaning: Continuous proximity to any runner behind within 5 m and 2.7 horse lanes; own rank changes reset the timer.
keys.limitation: Sample-held timer proxy; replacing a qualifying neighbor does not reset the timer.

gametora.reviewNote: Use the separate wider rear-proximity thresholds: 5 m and 2.7 horse lanes, with the same rank-reset rule.

keys.meaning: Recorded rushed-mode or front-block state.
Continuous front/side blocking timer.
keys.limitation: Front flag is recorded; timer is sampled. Side blocking is a geometric proxy, not a recorded state.

keys.meaning: Number of showdowns; current Global rules only ask whether at least one occurred.
keys.limitation: A recorded showdown proves >0; episode/resume counts beyond that remain unsupported.

gametora.reviewNote: The current Global tests only require at least one final-straight duel. A recorded start supports that; resume counting does not establish larger exact counts.

keys.meaning: Reference course segment at the observed distance; final-corner flag stays set into the final straight.

gametora.reviewNote: Use the named track corner on its last pass, not simply the first corner encountered in the race.

keys.meaning: 100 × (leader distance − own distance) / (leader distance − last distance).
keys.limitation: A zero field spread leaves the ratio undefined.

gametora.reviewNote: Use the leader gap divided by the full field spread, multiplied by 100. A zero spread does not supply a denominator.

keys.meaning: Whole metres behind the leader of the whole field; the separate float predicate uses decimetres.

gametora.reviewNote: Compare the whole-metre leader gap; this key is not the separate decimetre predicate.

keys.meaning: Entry into the last straight, detected from the sampled segment transition.
keys.limitation: The exact simulation-tick notification is absent; no arbitrary 10 m active region is invented.

gametora.reviewNote: Use the transition into the final straight, rather than treating the first 10 m as a lasting condition.

keys.meaning: Runner has reached the recorded final-spurt start distance.
Recent lane movement: 1 inward toward the fence, 2 outward; 0 means no sampled movement.
keys.limitation: Recorded lane changes show motion, not the exact simulation-tick transition.

gametora.reviewNote: Value 1 is movement inward and value 2 is movement outward; this is not a boolean for any lane movement.

keys.meaning: Another runner has just activated a beneficial effect of the specified type; Global value9 means healing.
keys.limitation: Same/preceding-tick healing notifications are inferred; missing events do not prove absence. Other effect values remain unsupported.

simulator.treatment: not declared in inspected simulator snapshot

gametora.reviewNote: Match a positive effect of the requested type on another runner. The Global value 9 is recovery, not any beneficial skill.

keys.meaning: Having an overtake target: a visible runner up to 20 m ahead, catchable within 15 seconds at current actual speeds.
keys.limitation: Visible faster-approach candidates are modeled; the selected target and timers are not recorded.

gametora.reviewNote: An overtaking candidate is ahead within 20 m and reachable within 15 s at current speeds; actual target selection is unrecorded.

keys.meaning: Nearby/surrounding opponents using longitudinal gaps and horse-lane width thresholds.
keys.limitation: Uses the documented course-width/18 horse-lane scale and reference spatial rules, not a recorded internal neighborhood.

gametora.reviewNote: Require front, rear and side occupancy. One neighbor may satisfy multiple roles; the side neighbor can be on either side.

keys.meaning: Recorded rushed-mode or front-block state.
Course-width lane class: 0 at <=0.2, 1 at <=0.4, 2 at <=0.6, otherwise 3.

gametora.reviewNote: Classify the lane using boundaries 0.2, 0.4 and 0.6, inclusive at each upper edge.

keys.meaning: HP-feasibility state: 0 cannot finish at base speed, 1 can exceed base but not sustain maximum, 2 can sustain maximum spurt.
keys.limitation: Reference budget state latches from late entry and recalculates on positive recovery; selected target and wit choice remain unreported.

gametora.reviewNote: Classify the HP budget as insufficient for base speed, sufficient for a reduced spurt, or sufficient for maximum spurt speed. Replay reconstruction is modeled evidence.
